description: How much will Nvidia's maximum potential guarantee liability under the SB Energy/OpenAI affiliate infrastructure leases be at its next annual report?
outcome: The maximum potential amount guaranteed, any amounts paid or accrued, and the remaining term of the guarantees disclosed in Nvidia's next annual report.
period: Nvidia's next annual report (fiscal year ending late January 2027), as fixed by the reason for an obligation already undertaken.

description: How much of Nvidia's $279 billion of supply and capacity commitments will remain outstanding or unconditional at its next annual report?
outcome: The total supply and capacity purchase commitments and the portion that is adjustable or cancelable at a cost, as disclosed in Nvidia's next annual report.
period: Nvidia's next annual report (fiscal year ending late January 2027), as fixed by the reason for an obligation already undertaken.

description: By how much will contract prices for AI-server memory (HBM/DRAM) — the memory input cost embedded in Nvidia's GPUs — rise or fall in calendar 2027?
outcome: The change in HBM/DRAM contract prices over calendar 2027, and the memory makers' reported average selling prices and memory gross margins for the periods covering 2027.
period: Calendar 2027 (overlapping Micron's fiscal 2027, roughly September 2026–August 2027), as supported by Micron management's fiscal 2027 price guidance in the October 6, 2026 article.

description: How much combined capital expenditure will the five largest hyperscalers — Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta Platforms and Oracle — spend in calendar 2026 and calendar 2027?
outcome: The big five hyperscalers' combined capex for calendar 2026 and calendar 2027, versus the approximately $800 billion for 2026 and roughly $1.3 trillion for 2027 the article reports they plan to spend.
period: Calendar 2026 and calendar 2027 (the two years the Oct. 6, 2026 article gives), settled at the hyperscalers' quarterly earnings releases reporting capex through the fourth quarter of 2027.

description: Will Nvidia complete its approximately $12.93 billion acquisition of Hugging Face — and at what final cost and regulatory conditions — by the check date?
outcome: Closing or termination of the signed Hugging Face acquisition, the final consideration paid (roughly $11.9 billion to shareholders plus up to $1 billion of equity-based retention awards), and any conditions regulators impose.
period: Check date: the first half of calendar 2027, the closing window the Sept. 3, 2026 agreement states (within 18 months of the Oct. 6, 2026 item).

description: Will the U.S. licence requirement on Nvidia's data center chips still bar it from China's data center compute market at Nvidia's fiscal 2027 year-end, or will it be lifted before then?
outcome: Whether the U.S. export-licence requirement on Nvidia's H20-class data center products remains in force or is lifted, and whether Nvidia resumes recognizing data center compute revenue from China.
period: Nvidia's fiscal year ending late January 2027 (current fiscal year-end, the date fixed for the pending export-control status).

description: Will Nvidia's Rubin data center GPU — the next generation of the product that carries Nvidia's data center revenue — reach volume ramp in the quarter management describes, or slip into calendar 2027 because of memory shortages?
outcome: Whether Rubin's volume ramp and shipments occur in the quarter Nvidia describes (about 20% of data center revenue) or are pushed into calendar 2027, and whether reported sales timing slips.
period: Check date: Nvidia's fiscal Q3 FY2027 report (~November 2026) and fiscal Q4 FY2027 report (~February 2027), which will show whether the Rubin ramp landed by the quarter ending late January 2027 or slid into calendar 2027, the two points the item frames ('this quarter' versus 'slip into 2027').

description: How much residual-value/loss-share exposure has Nvidia taken on under its customer data center financing support — the commitment to cover up to 25% of the loss if financed chips lose value — and how much is disclosed at its next annual report?
outcome: The maximum potential amount of Nvidia's loss coverage on customer data center chip values, any amounts paid or accrued, and the terms and remaining duration of that support, as disclosed in Nvidia's next annual report.
period: Nvidia's next annual report (fiscal year ending late January 2027), as fixed by the reason for an obligation already undertaken.

description: Will Nvidia's Groq 3 LPX rack-scale LPU system — the first product built on the Groq technology it paid about $20 billion to license and staff — reach volume shipments and commercial scale in the quarter Nvidia describes (its fiscal Q3 FY2027), or slip?
outcome: Whether Groq 3 LPX volume shipments occur 'later this quarter' as Nvidia stated, and whether the system begins contributing to reported data center revenue or slips into fiscal Q4 FY2027/calendar 2027.
period: Check date: Nvidia's fiscal Q3 FY2027 report (~November 2026) confirming shipments in the quarter Nvidia described in the Oct. 8, 2026 item; if unconfirmed there, the fiscal Q4 FY2027 report (~February 2027) fixes the slip.

description: What will the hourly spot rental price for Nvidia B200 GPUs be at the end of calendar 2026, after more than doubling from March 2026 to October 2026?
outcome: The hourly spot rental price for Nvidia B200 GPUs at year-end 2026 and whether it remains above its March 2026 level.
period: Calendar 2026, settled by Ornn's published GPU rental index releases through year-end 2026 (the Oct. 10, 2026 article gives the March-to-October 2026 move).

description: Will Nvidia sign and complete an acquisition of Reflection AI — and at what consideration and terms — by the check date?
outcome: A definitive agreement to acquire Reflection AI, its closing (or the talks' collapse), and the final consideration paid and any regulatory conditions imposed.
period: Check date: April 2028, the outer limit of a date within 18 months of the Oct. 10, 2026 item for an acquisition not yet signed.

description: How much will global AI capital spending total in calendar 2026 and calendar 2027?
outcome: Global AI capex for calendar 2026 and calendar 2027, measured against Goldman Sachs' forecast of $1 trillion of global AI spend this year and AI spend equal to 1.8% of U.S. GDP in 2026, 2.5% in 2027 (and 2.8% in 2028).
period: Calendar 2026 and calendar 2027 (with 2028 also given), the years Goldman Sachs' forecast in the Oct. 11, 2026 article covers.

description: How much of Nvidia's $25 billion of equity-investment commitments outstanding at July 26, 2026 will be funded or remain outstanding at its next annual report?
outcome: The remaining balance of Nvidia's equity-investment commitments, the cash paid to fund them, and any change in the committed amounts, as disclosed in Nvidia's next annual report.
period: Nvidia's next annual report (fiscal year ending late January 2027), as fixed by the reason for an obligation already undertaken.
